findings.detail: VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN is a valid JWT exposing: project=alter-ego, owner=damilolas-projects-fafdf859, environment=development, owner_id=team_WiDBceN6VoOQgdZ2jORoLLwN, user_id=GLHPNMf9TIgdZ7d96gCSIFOz, client_id=cl_HYyOPBNtFMfHhaUn9L4QPfTZz6TP47bp. EXPIRES: 2026-07-16. This token was auto-injected by Vercel CLI and grants access to Vercel resources.
findings.risk: Token in plaintext in .env.local. If committed or shared, grants Vercel deployment access.
findings.mitigation: Add .env.local to .gitignore (verify), rotate the OIDC token via Vercel dashboard.

findings.detail: No Content-Security-Policy headers configured. No helmet, no security middleware.
findings.risk: XSS, clickjacking, and MIME-sniffing attacks not mitigated at HTTP header level.
findings.mitigation: Add CSP headers in next.config.ts headers() config.

findings.detail: POST /api/analyze accepts any JSON body without schema validation. body.addresses is iterated without checking array bounds, address format, or chain validity.
findings.risk: Malformed input could cause unhandled errors (caught by generic catch → 500). No injection risk since only iterated and passed to OnchainOS CLI.
findings.mitigation: Add Zod schema validation for AnalyzeRequest.

findings.detail: No rate limiting on any API endpoint. Anonymous users can hammer all 4 endpoints.
findings.risk: DoS possible via repeated requests. Low impact for hackathon demo.
findings.mitigation: Add Vercel rate limiting or middleware-based throttle.

findings.detail: All 4 API endpoints are public — no auth tokens, API keys, or session checks.
findings.risk: Any internet user can call analyze/roast/compare/persona. Low risk since demo uses pre-cached data.
findings.mitigation: Add x402 payment gate or API key for post-demo production.

summary: 1 P0 (Vercel OIDC token in .env.local), 1 P1 (no CSP), 2 P2 (no input validation, rate limiting), 1 P3 (no auth). .env.example is clean.
